I've held a Curio and Relics 03 FFL (US) for many years now and am a collector of that class of firearms. I've searched about frequently and have found no firearms related subverses that appear to fit that hobby/interest group. My question is simply, what is your opinion of me creating a new subverse that would cater to this small niche?

My guess is that there wouldn't be many interested and it would be a rather small sub. However, it is not my intent to take anything from any existing firearms type subs, all are quite good here on Voat, but simply to augment existing ones. It is also not my intent to create something that already exists, and I just haven't found it. I'm relatively new, but active on Voat, so it is possible I simply missed one. If anyone knows of a sub that would fit this concept, please feel free to inform me.

Anyway, the proposed sub would be dedicated to those of us who collect older weapons. My thought is that it would contain information on historical firearms, gun collecting (possible a full range of older weapons) in general, along with provide advice and assistance for those wishing to enter the hobby or navigate the paperwork involved in being licensed. Your thoughts on this subject would be greatly appreciated.
I'd love to know more. I'm not an ffl holder, but would love to know what interesting and fun things I could get if I did become one. Discussion would be welcome. Go to town!

It's actually quite interesting ... in general, anything older than fifty years is considered a collectable firearm and the cost of the FFL is quite low. Assuming you qualify to buy a firearm normally, you basically qualify for a C&R, the cost of which is $30 every 3 years. It allows you to buy online from places like Gunbroker.com or any of the dealers or sites which deal in such things, just as any FFL holder can, with the exception of the age of weapon purchased and a few variables. It is a legitimate BATF issued firearms license, just as any other.
